about: Built-in rule set of the project generator: every number a decision depends on. Layers override the value in this order: built-in, norm pack, preset, project, brief/chat. `alias` is the older brief field that reads and writes the same rule. `default: null` means the typology preset decides. Lengths are metres, areas m2, angles degrees. `why`: what the rule decides and the norm or reason behind its default.

rules.why: Depth of one band of rooms behind its facade: a room deeper than 12 m is not lit from it. A data hall takes dc.hall_band instead.
Target width of one patch of a free-form shell along the facade and across the roof; each patch is one surface that can be made, shipped and glazed on its own.
Stand-off of the shell skin from the slab edge at the floor and at the eaves; the least clear gap for drainage, fixings and cleaning behind the glass.
How far the skin swells out from the slab edge at the middle of its height, where it is widest; with the wave it makes the facade curve in both directions.
Largest outward lean of the skin towards the eaves, varying along the facade in waves; a lean over the walk-way gives shade.
Waves of the swell, the lean and the eaves round the whole outline; one wave per patch group keeps the panels repeatable.
Half the range of the eaves height along the outline: the roof edge rises and falls by this much round the building.
Rise of the roof from its eaves to the central opening; it gives the roof its second curvature across the span.
Radius of the central roof opening as a share of the nearest distance from the centre to the outline; it is closed by the glazed dome over the atrium.
Rise of the glazed dome over the central opening as a share of the opening radius; 1.0 is a hemisphere.

Target width of a glass panel along the facade; the count is rounded up so no panel is wider. The planarising gap grows with the panel area: 1.5 x 1.8 m left 0.029 m, over the 0.02 m cold-bend limit, and 0.9 x 1.1 m left corners 0.0117 m off the surface (limit 0.01); 0.8 x 1.0 m holds both, at about 3.4 times the panels of 1.5 x 1.8 m.
Target height of a glass panel; the count is rounded up so no panel is taller. Sized with massing.shell_panel_w so every panel cold-bends on the frame.
Largest gap between the diagonals of a quad panel still made as flat glass; a glazier's tolerance.
Largest diagonal gap of a panel that can be cold-bent on the frame; beyond it the panel is hot-bent and costs more.
Rounds of planar-quad optimisation that move the panel corners towards flat glass while they stay on the surface; zero keeps the raw grid.
Depth of the steel rib that follows the surface along each patch edge, up the skin and over the roof.
Total thickness of the shell roof build-up (deck, insulation, cladding) measured along the surface normal.
Share of the radius of curvature the skin may stand out where the outline is concave, so the offset surface does not fold over itself.
Share of its depth a rib sits behind the surface it follows, so the glass and the roof cover it.
Width of a rib as a share of its depth.
Share of the roof build-up thickness taken by the structural deck.
Share of the roof build-up thickness taken by insulation; the cladding takes the rest.
Thickness of the glass of a skin panel.
Width of the mullion along every panel edge.
Depth of the mullion along every panel edge.
Outer diameter of the tube of the dome diagrid; the section is taken from the catalogue by diameter and wall.
Wall thickness of the tube of the dome diagrid.
Where the swell of the skin peaks along the outline, as an angle of the wave; keeps swell, lean and eaves from peaking together.
Where the lean of the skin peaks along the outline, as an angle of the wave.
Share of the height at which the skin is widest.
Most patches (skin and roof) of a shell; wider patches are taken beyond it, so the element count stays inside the project's slots.
Radius of curvature above which a direction counts as flat; a patch curved both ways under it is double-curved.
Least clear gap of the skin from the slab edge as a share of the stand-off rule; a shell that comes closer is refused.
Clear height wanted above the roof level where roof plant stands; the eaves are raised until the roof clears it.
Greatest storey height over column side; a taller storey gets a thicker column. Design choice before the structural design.
Column sides are rounded up to a whole step of this size, the module of formwork and precast sections; design choice.
Clear width of a stair flight and its landings. The typology sets it; a country minimum raises it, a width the brief names stays.
Least flight width a country allows inside one dwelling; a house stair is never built narrower.

Highest step riser. The generator keeps 0.18 m unless a stricter country limit applies. The range goes up to 0.23 m, the steepest dwelling stair a shipped pack allows (jp, Building Standard Law Enforcement Order art. 23).
Depth of the anteroom in front of an operating theatre, taken from the corridor side over the theatre's whole width: staff scrub and the trolley turns there, and the theatre has no other door.
Smallest foyer a brief may ask for: a room where people wait, meet and queue at the entrance, with space for coats and a doorway at each side; a smaller one is a lobby corner.
Smallest gallery (a wide through-room to walk along and look at things): narrower than about 2.5 m in plan it is a corridor.
Smallest atrium: a roofed, daylit hall several storeys high; a smaller one is a lightwell and takes no seating or circulation.
Apartments on one floor when the footprint width is not fixed. With a width given, the limit follows it: room.apartment_frontage of facade per apartment, on both sides of the corridor.
Facade length one apartment needs to light a living room and a bedroom side by side; with the footprint width it gives how many apartments a floor holds.

Which doors open in the direction of escape. none: every leaf swings into the room it serves. exit: exterior exit doors open outward and stair doors open into the stair. route: also the doors of public rooms from the floor area in opening.out_swing_area up, towards the exit.
Floor area from which a public room is taken to hold enough people for its door to open outward, with the route; design choice, a proxy for the occupant load a country sets.
Least width left free in a corridor beside a leaf that swings into it. A door whose leaf would leave less swings into its own room instead; an exit direction on a stair or exterior door is kept.
Frame and leaf thickness taken off an opening's width to get the clear passage; design choice (common practice).

Least clear passage of a door on the accessible route: entrances, flat doors, doors of public rooms. A door narrower is widened about its centre when the wall leaves room. 0 asks nothing until a country pack sets it.
Least clear passage of an exit door and a stair door. A narrower door is widened about its centre when the wall leaves room. 0 asks nothing until a country pack sets it.
Fire resistance (EI minutes) of a door in the wall of a stair core. The wall and its doors take the same class; 0 builds a plain door.
Fire resistance (EI minutes) of a flat entrance door: a door between a dwelling and a common room.
Fire resistance (EI minutes) of a door to a lift landing or a technical room.
Fire resistance (EI minutes) of a door in a wall between two dwellings, the wall that separates fire compartments.
Least sound reduction of a flat entrance door; design choice.
Least sound reduction of a window or exterior door; design choice for an ordinary street.
Highest thermal transmittance of a window or exterior door. A country pack sets its envelope limit; a stricter value picks the triple glazed type.

Which species groups the site trees are drawn from: the types of the Tree family in the library carry a group and a weight, data/tree_mix.json says which groups a mix takes. Only the look and the shade change, not the count.

The season the site trees stand in: the library Tree types carry a Season, so autumn trees turn red, gold or brown, winter ones are bare and spring ones are in young leaf or blossom; evergreens stay as they are. Only the look changes, not the count.
Whether a site with paving or trees also gets its landscape: a hedge along the plot boundary, beds with shrubs outside the paving, lawn on the open ground, and paths from the entrances to the street.
The side of the plot the street lies on; the paths lead to it, the street tree row stands along it and the hedge opens for the paths there.
Width of the free ground between the paving and the plot boundary where the hedge stands; it grows when the trees need more room.
The side of the plot the hedge runs on: all four, the street side, or one named side. A brief that puts the hedge "along the street" or on a named edge sets it.
The hedge along the plot boundary: none, a clipped 1.2 m hedge, a low 0.6 m one, a tall 1.8 m screen or a 2 m conifer hedge. It opens where a path leaves the plot.
Width of the planting bed outside the paving; shrubs from the library Shrub family stand in it. Zero leaves no bed.
Width of the paths from the entrances to the street, in paving slabs of 1.5 m.
Least clear trunk under the crown of a site tree, so people and cars pass under it however the tree is scaled; kept below 0.4 of the tree's height.

Which species the site trees are: bit i set plants the i-th species of data/tree_mix.json `species` (oak, birch, maple, ...); 0 leaves it to site.tree_mix. The brief's words ("oaks and birches", in English, Russian or German) set it.
How much the size of each site tree may differ from its species type, up or down, as a share of the type; seeded per tree, so a site keeps its trees. 0 plants every tree at the size of its type.

Least gap between the crown of a site tree, at its own scaled size, and the building: its walls and the eaves of its roof (the roof overhang counted). A crown that would come nearer is scaled down, and a tree that cannot keep the gap is left out.
Least distance from the building outline to a tree trunk, so that crowns and roots stay clear of the walls.
Least free distance between a tree trunk and the edge of a path tile.
Rows of trees along the street edge of the plot, along the last stretch of each path to the street, or both; they come from the same tree mix and are added to the count of site trees.
Distance between the trees of a row along the street or a path.
Set-back of a plot edge on a street: room for the pavement, entrances and the fire appliance's working strip.
Least set-back of a plot edge that is not on a street; spacing and sun push it further where a neighbour needs it.
Least clear distance between two buildings of a block: fire spread and privacy. Each side of a shared plot edge keeps half.
Clear distance to a neighbour as a share of the taller one's height: daylight and shadow between buildings. A tall neighbour lowers the storeys when the plots are too small for it.
Farthest a building may stand from a street: a fire appliance must reach a facade. A plot farther from every street is refused.
Floor area the block aims for per plot area; the storeys of each building follow from it and its buildable area.
Fewest storeys a building of the block gets from the floor-area target or the sun rule.
Most storeys a building of the block gets from the floor-area target.
Narrowest buildable area left by the set-backs; less and the tallest building next to it loses a storey.
How close a plot edge must lie to a street or to another plot to count as on it.
Height above the top storey that the spacing and sun rules count: roof deck and parapet.
Program of a plot on two streets that meet: a corner takes the busier use.
Program of every other plot.
Length of the platform: the longest train that stops plus a stopping margin; design choice, the operator's train length decides it.
Width of an island platform between its two edges; it holds the escalator, stair and lift wells with a walking lane each side; design choice.
Clear walking lane kept between a well and the platform edge, and between wells along the platform; design choice.
From the platform edge to the inside face of the box wall: the vehicle with its clearance and an escape walkway; design choice.
Depth of the top of rail below the ground; the line's alignment decides it.
Platform floor above the top of rail, level with the train floor; design choice.
From the top of rail down to the top of the base slab: rails, sleepers and the track slab; design choice.
Soil over the roof slab: room for street services, paving and planting; design choice.
Thickness of the roof slab carrying the soil cover and the street; design choice before the structural design.
Thickness of the base slab under the tracks, which also holds the box down against ground water; design choice.
Thickness of the concourse and platform slabs; design choice.
From the concourse floor to the underside of the roof slab: headroom, signs and the services above the ceiling; design choice.
Least clear height from the platform to the underside of the concourse slab; design choice.
Length of the plant zone at each end of the box beyond the platform: fans, substation, pumps; design choice.
Thinnest diaphragm wall, the smallest common grab width; design choice.
Diaphragm wall thickness per metre of excavation depth; a first sizing before the geotechnical design.
Steps the wall thickness and the shaft sizes are rounded up to; design choice.
Embedment of the diaphragm wall below the formation, as a share of the excavation depth; a first sizing before the geotechnical design.
People per hour that leave the platform in the peak; the ridership forecast decides it.
Practical capacity of one escalator; design choice for a one-metre step band.
Banks of escalators between the platform and the concourse, spread along the platform; design choice.
Escalators in each bank beyond the peak flow, so one can stop for repair; design choice.
Slope of the escalators; design choice, the common incline.
Width an escalator takes in its well, balustrades included; design choice.
Flat length at each end of an escalator well: the landing and the machine pit; design choice.
Width of the fixed stair beside each bank of escalators; design choice, the exit width a country pack asks for replaces it.
Highest riser of the station stairs; design choice for heavy public use.
Thickness of the stair flight slab; design choice.
Gap between the two flights of a station stair turning on its landing; design choice.
People a metre of stair width carries up per minute in an evacuation; design choice.
People one full train brings to the platform; the rolling stock decides it.
Longest time to clear two full trains off the platform; design choice, a country pack's evacuation time replaces it.
1 fits platform screen doors along both platform edges, one at each train door; 0 leaves the edges open. Design choice for passenger safety.
Height of the platform screen above the platform. Design choice.
Clear width of a platform screen door; wider than the train door so a stopping error still lines up. Design choice.
Distance between train doors along a car; one screen door is placed per pitch of platform. Design choice.
Lifts from the platform to the street, for step-free access; design choice.
Side of a lift shaft; design choice for a stretcher-sized car.
Rated load of a station lift; the car is the library type of that load, a stretcher fits from 1000 kg; design choice.
Air the tunnel ventilation moves through each end of the station; design choice before the ventilation study.
Air speed in a ventilation shaft; design choice that keeps noise and pressure loss low.
Longest distance between the columns on the platform centreline; design choice.
Rise of each tunnel barrel vault over the span it covers; design choice, the crown stays under the concourse slab.
Lowest springing of a tunnel vault above the platform; design choice, the clear height of a person plus the screen doors.
Longest length of one vault segment along the tracks; design choice, one segment per structural bay.
How far the ground plane reaches beyond the box walls; design choice.
Side of a square station column; design choice before the structural design.

Band lays rooms along a full-length corridor; free searches end rooms, runs and zones so the corridor is only as long as the doors need; auto builds both and keeps the better one that passes the gates.
Grid step the free layout snaps the footprint length to.
Branch-and-bound nodes of the free layout per floor: more finds better plans, slower.
Neighbourhood rebuild rounds after the search: each takes a few rooms out and puts them back cheaper.
Wall-time cap of the free layout search of one zone (floor or apartment) once a plan is found; 0 for none. A cap that cuts the search makes the plan depend on the machine's speed.
Free layout objective: cost of a square metre of corridor; the unit the other layout costs are weighed against.
Free layout objective: cost of a square metre a room takes beyond its asked area.
Free layout objective: cost of a square metre a hall or lobby takes beyond its asked area; it is circulation, weighed as corridor.
Free layout objective: cost of a square metre of a store made of a leftover too short for a window.
Free layout objective: cost of a square metre of a spare room made of a leftover with a window.
Design critique rounds on a new project before it is drafted: each fills a design field the brief left open and rebuilds; 0 drafts the brief as given.

How a free apartment section reaches its flats: a corridor with flats on both sides and round its ends, or a gallery along the north facade with flats on one side; auto keeps the better plan that passes.
Sun orientation of the flats of a free section: south keeps flats off the north side of the corridor, so none faces north only: each has a room on the south facade or an end facade.
Sort the ceiling void into bands by system, each at a set depth under the slab soffit, so runs of different systems do not cross. Off keeps each system's own elevation.
Cable tray: axis depth under the slab soffit when the void layers are on; design choice, ducts keep the top band.
Cold and hot water mains: axis depth under the slab soffit when the void layers are on; design choice, ducts keep the top band.
Heating pipes: axis depth under the slab soffit when the void layers are on; design choice, ducts keep the top band.
Chilled water pipes: axis depth under the slab soffit when the void layers are on; design choice, ducts keep the top band.
Sprinkler branch row: axis depth under the slab soffit when the void layers are on; design choice, ducts keep the top band.

A storey under a wet storey that asked for no wet rooms takes the stack's toilets on the same risers: the drain runs through it anyway, so the toilets cost no new riser, and a storey people work on needs one.
A wet room further than this from a wet room on the storey below needs a drain run along the slab instead of a straight riser; past it the stack counts as broken.
Shafts and columns line up storey over storey within this; a shaft that moves is a new shaft, a column that moves needs a transfer beam.
Columns allowed to stand on no column below, each on a transfer beam; every one is extra structure and depth in the slab.
Window glass of a lit room as a share of its floor; below it the room is dim in daytime.
Daylight from one wall reaches about 2 to 3 window head heights into a room; a lit room deeper than this ratio times its window head is dark at the back.
Largest kitchen without a window of its own: a niche opening to a lit living room and drawn through a mechanical extract. A larger kitchen needs a facade window; 0 asks every kitchen to have one.
On: a guard rail on both sides of every stair flight and along every floor void edge no wall lines; off leaves them to be drawn by hand.
Height of a guard rail above the floor or the stair pitch line where the floor drops away.
Narrowest floor opening that is a void to guard; a smaller one is a service penetration closed by its cover.
On: rails the deck of a flat roof inside a parapet lower than the guard height, for maintenance access; off leaves the roof to anchor points.
Longest way from the farthest point of a room to an exit: the entrance doors on the ground floor, a stair door above. Norm packs set the value of their country.
Clear width of a common corridor or lobby, so a wheelchair and a person on foot pass.
Width of a door off a common route, so a wheelchair goes through it.
Turning circle of a wheelchair: every storey with a common route has a place on it this wide.
Floor area one fire compartment may hold: a storey larger than this needs fire walls or a smaller plate.
Building height above ground from which the generator fits an automatic sprinkler system when the brief does not say. Norm packs set the limit of their country; the brief's own yes or no wins.
Floor area one sprinkler head covers: the head grid is laid so no head serves more. The design density times this area is the flow of one head.
Greatest distance between two heads on a branch and between branches; design choice inside the usual 4.6 m ceiling of the standards.
Greatest distance from a head to a wall; a head further than this leaves the corner uncovered, so the grid is moved or another head is added.
Least distance from a head to a wall, so the spray is not blocked.
Distance of a pendent head inlet below the slab soffit above it, in the ceiling void; design choice.
Height of a branch pipe axis above the inlet of the heads hung from it: the length of each head drop; design choice.
Smallest sprinkler pipe: drops, branches and mains never go below this nominal size, whatever their flow; design choice.
Design water density over the covered floor; with the head area it gives the flow of one head (litres per minute).
Heads assumed to open together: a main or riser is sized for this many at most, however many it feeds.
Highest water speed in a sprinkler pipe; each run takes the smallest catalogue pipe that keeps its flow under it.
Most heads on one branch line before a second branch starts; keeps the branch pipe small and the friction loss low.
Floor area one sprinkler riser serves on a storey; a larger plate takes more risers.
Fewest risers of the sprinkler system, so one riser out of service leaves the other storeys' supply; they stand in the core, apart.
Height of one pressure zone of the sprinkler riser: above it a pump set feeds the next zone, so no head sees a static pressure over the pipe class.
Building height from which protected stairs are pressurised against smoke: a fan on the roof feeds each stair shaft. Norm packs set their country's limit.

Light hazard: Greatest floor area one head serves in this class; the grid is laid so no head serves more. The default lies in the usual range of the sprinkler standards for this class; the ordinary class reads the fire.head_spacing, fire.head_area, fire.head_wall_max and fire.density rules.

Light hazard: Greatest distance between two heads on a branch and between branches in this class. The default lies in the usual range of the sprinkler standards for this class; the ordinary class reads the fire.head_spacing, fire.head_area, fire.head_wall_max and fire.density rules.

Light hazard: Greatest distance from a head to a wall in this class; also how far a head reaches along each plan axis when coverage is measured. The default lies in the usual range of the sprinkler standards for this class; the ordinary class reads the fire.head_spacing, fire.head_area, fire.head_wall_max and fire.density rules.

Light hazard: Design water density of this class; with the area per head it gives the flow of one head. The default lies in the usual range of the sprinkler standards for this class; the ordinary class reads the fire.head_spacing, fire.head_area, fire.head_wall_max and fire.density rules.

Distance of a pendent head's deflector below the ceiling face: the head shows under the ceiling so the spray is not held in the void; design choice inside the usual range.
Least clear distance of a branch line, room trunk or head from a column face; the head rows move past a column, or grow denser, to keep it.
Height of the top storey floor above ground from which every stair core gets a standpipe with landing valves for the fire service. Norm packs set the limit of their country.
Distance of the standpipe axis from the two walls of the stair corner it stands in; design choice for fixing and access.
Design flow of one standpipe: the riser takes the smallest catalogue pipe that carries it under the speed rule. Norm packs set the flow of their country.
Smallest standpipe riser, whatever its flow; design choice.
Design flow of one landing valve and its branch; the branch is sized for it.
Smallest branch to a landing valve, the usual hose valve size; design choice.
Height of the landing valve outlet above the storey floor, within reach of a standing person; norm packs set it.
Length of the branch from the standpipe to its landing valve along the wall; design choice that keeps the tee and the valve apart.
Least distance of the standpipe and its landing valve from a door opening of the stair, so neither blocks the way out.
Rise of the standpipe above its top landing valve to the closed end with the air valve; design choice.
Farthest point of a protected room from a landing valve of its storey, measured along the plan axes as a hose is laid: hose length plus the jet. Norm packs set it.
Most storeys of a house; a house taller than this is another typology.
Most storeys of a school block.
Most storeys of an apartment section or an office; the limit is the building height rule below, not a count.
Greatest height of the roof above ground that the site's zoning, airspace or norm allows. The storey count is the least of this height over the storey height and the typology's count.

A brief that lists a curtain wall or glazed facade among its features, and names no facade system itself, gets the curtain system: real curtain wall elements with mullions, panels and spandrels instead of wall bays with large windows.

A brief that lists timber, CLT or glulam among its features, and names no structure itself, gets a timber structure: glulam columns on the grid with CLT floors for a frame, CLT walls and floors otherwise.
Spacing of the vertical mullions of a curtain wall; each bay between two mullions holds one panel per row.
Height of the opaque spandrel band of a curtain wall above the floor slab: it hides the slab edge and the fire stop behind. 0 makes the wall glass over the full storey.
